newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, JADEJA IN ONSLAUGHT V S AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR, JADEJA IN ONSLAUGHT V S AFRICA.

text.p: A charmed century by skipper Sachin Tendulkar and a late burst by Ajay Jadeja helped India to an imposing 267for six in 50 overs in the one-off one-day cricket match against South Africa on Saturday.

In an eventful first session, marked by a protest walkout by the South Africans against unruly crowd behaviour, Tendulkar scored his 10th one-day century during his 133rd outing after winning the toss and electing to bat on an easy wicket.
Tendulkar rode his luck after Herschelle Gibbs dropped him at point off Brian Mcmillan when he was on three.
He went on to score 114 off 126 balls, a knock studded with 14 boundaries, before he was stumped by makeshift wicket-keeper Gary Kirsten as he stepped out to a short delivery from Nicky Boje.

Earlier play was held up for 20 minutes after former skipper and in-form batsman Mohammad Azharuddin was given out caught behind by Kirsten, though the rising ball off Derek Crookes seemed to have hit his left pad.
The decision triggered unrest among spectators who threw water satchels at spinner Paul Adams fielding at square leg, resulting in a walkout by the South Africans, led by skipper Hansie Cronje.
An appeal by Azharuddin calmed the protestors and play resumed after 20 minutes.
Azharuddin's exit and Tendulkar's dismissal caused a slump in the Indian innings, the run rate falling below five runs an over. India scored only 15 runs between 41st and 45th over.
But a fierce 54 off 44 balls by Jadeja boosted India's score to a challenging total.
Jadeja's unbeaten knock contained two fours and four sixes, with the last two overs of the Indian innings yielding 34 runs. The worst sufferers were spinners Pat Symcox and Adams.
South Africa needed to score 268 or 5.36 runs an over to win the match.
